candidate.title: Every Fully Composable Homomorphic Encryption Scheme Yields a Circular-Secure One
candidate.informal: Bootstrapping turns a non-composable homomorphic encryption scheme into a fully composable one at the cost of a circular security assumption. The conjecture is the converse: that a fully composable scheme can always be turned back into a circular-secure one, so that circular security is necessary and not merely sufficient for full composability.
candidate.formal_statement_latex: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a set of functions. If there exists a valid, IND-CPA secure, fully composable $\mathcal{F}$-homomorphic encryption scheme, then there exist an injective key encoding $\psi$ and a valid, $\psi$-circular IND-CPA secure encryption scheme, which may be constructed from and depend on the former.
candidate.printed_statement: Conjecture 1: Any fully composable homomorphic encryption scheme can be modified into a circular secure one.
candidate.status_note: Printed as `Conjecture 1' in the source's concluding Section 6 (p. 19), as the way to address the displayed Question `Is circular security necessary necessary to achieve full composability?'. The converse direction is the source's own Theorem 6. No partial result and no counterexample is offered for this direction.
candidate.risks: The printed conjecture is one English sentence and fixes no quantifiers; the formal statement above is this page's reading and is flagged as such in Remark 1 of the draft. Three choices were made that the source does not make: that the conclusion is the existence of a circular-secure scheme rather than a property of the original; that the key encoding psi is existentially quantified; and that the constructed scheme need not be homomorphic. A reader who chooses differently is working on a different statement.

grounding.quote: Conjecture 1: Any fully composable homomorphic encryption scheme can be modified into a circular secure one.
Question: Is circular security necessary necessary to achieve full composability?

Note that the question does not make any reference to encryption noise, and all concepts (circular security, homomorphic encryption and full composability) have well formalized abstract cryptographic definitions. A possible way to address this question could be to show the following.

In fact, one could ask if any fully composable homomorphic encryption scheme is already circular secure, but this is most likely false as one can adapt the simple counterexamples demonstrating the existence of circular insecure encryption schemes to the fully composable setting.

So, the circular secure scheme of Conjecture 1 can be different from (but still depend on) the original composable FHE scheme. Given that circular security implies full composability (Theorem 6), proving the conjecture would show that circular security and full composability are essentially equivalent
for all keys (sk, pk) ← Gen(κ), function f : Mw → M in F, and ciphertexts c ∈ C w such that Dec∗ (sk, c) ∈ Mw .

verify.reason: The conjecture is printed verbatim in the source and is genuinely left open there; the only real defect in a draft of it is that the source states no quantifiers, so any formal version is supplied rather than quoted. The draft therefore prints the source's sentence as Conjecture 1 and its own formalization as a separately numbered Conjecture 2, with the choices listed in a remark.

checks.name: existence
checks.finding: Printed as a displayed, labelled conjecture in Section 6.

checks.name: openness
checks.finding: Section 6 is the paper's last section before the references; the conjecture is posed there and nothing later addresses it. Read forward to the end of the paper (p. 20) to confirm.

checks.name: strength
checks.finding: The draft does not strengthen: it prints the sentence as-is, and its formalization asks only for existence of some circular-secure scheme, which is the weakest reading consistent with the source's own gloss that the scheme 'can be different from (but still depend on) the original'.

checks.name: quantifiers
checks.finding: The source supplies none. The draft's Remark 1 lists the three choices it makes and says they are not the source's.

checks.name: attribution
checks.finding: The paper's own conjecture, not one it cites; the circular-security counterexamples it points to are attributed to others in the draft as well.

checks.name: definitions
checks.finding: Full composability is the source's Definition 6 and is reproduced clause for clause, including the quantification over all ciphertexts c with Dec*(sk,c) in M^w. psi-circular IND-CPA security is its Definition 3.

checks.name: fabrication
checks.finding: Every claim about the source in the draft's setting section is quoted or paraphrased from pp. 18-20. The remark that the formalization is non-vacuous only in the Impagliazzo-worlds sense is the draft's own and is marked as such.

checks.name: self-containment
checks.finding: The printed conjecture alone is not enough to know what to prove; the draft's Conjecture 2 plus Definitions 1-5 are, under the reading it states.

corrections.problem: The source states no formal version, so presenting one as the source's would misattribute it.
corrections.corrected: Print the source's sentence as its own numbered conjecture and the formalization as a second one, with a remark naming every choice made.

corrections.problem: Calling the conjecture 'open' without saying that the converse is a theorem of the same paper understates what is known.
corrections.corrected: Status line records Theorem 6 as the settled direction.
